newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - May 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - May 7.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on May 7. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

The head of the Surakarta branch of the minority United Development Party (PPP), Mudrick Setiawan Sangidoe, has met ousted Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) Megawati Sukarnoputri in an apparent bid by the Moslem-oriented PPP to woo disenchanted Megawati supporters away from the government-backed PDI faction.

The Indonesian government has frozen the activities of Canada's Bre-X Minerals Ltd and its subsidaries and is set to tighten rules on gold prospecting a day after the company revealed its Busang gold find in East Kalimantan was a hoax.
The ruling Golkar party general chairman Harmoko has pledged his political grouping will win public sympathy by campaigning for the May 29 election in an orderly fashion.
Indonesian armed forces spokesman Brigadier-General Slamet Supriadi said campaign-related traffic accidents had killed 30 people across the country since campaigning began on April 27.
Indonesian police will soon form a team to investigate the Bre-X gold hoax and intend to question both past and present officials of the Mines and Energy Department.

Mines and Energy Minister Ida Bagus Sudjana said the Indonesian government is seeking a 10 percent stake in PT Newmont Nusa Tenggara, which controls 80 percent of the Batu Hijau project in West Nusa Tenggara province.
